comparator.name: Sociale geografie en planologie
comparator.academicYear: Current curriculum for prospective cohorts after 2026, checked 2026-09-28
comparator.sourceNotes: The official current curriculum accounts for 180 EC. Year 1 is a fixed 60-EC foundation of eight 7.5-EC courses. The generic target names no track, so the first-listed Migratie en mondiale ontwikkeling track is selected by neutral official order: four 7.5-EC track courses (30 EC). Two first-listed SGPL electives supply 15 EC of major choice. The programme states that students take two SGPL electives in the major and otherwise use profiling space; the remaining 45 EC of profiling space is kept genuinely open. Year 3 closes with three 5-EC research-and-context courses and a 15-EC bachelor thesis. The resulting pathway totals 60 EC foundation + 45 EC selected major + 45 EC profiling + 30 EC final research semester = 180 EC.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names none of the four equally formal thematic tracks. Migratie en mondiale ontwikkeling is listed first on the official curriculum page, so it is selected neutrally before UCR fit is considered. The first-listed eligible SGPL electives instantiate the two required major electives; genuine profiling space remains open.

alternatives.label: Cities, people & spatial sustainability
alternatives.concept: Combines social-science analysis of people, institutions, inequality and urban change with environmental systems, spatial data, earth observation, economics and applied sustainability research to understand and improve places.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum joins urban and social analysis to spatial-environmental methods and sustainability; the label does not imply that UCR offers a dedicated professional planning degree.
progression: Social-science, sustainability, data and research foundations precede advanced urban inequality, environmental governance, earth observation, econometrics and applied research. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Globalisation, migration & transnational places
alternatives.concept: Studies how empire, globalisation, migration, political institutions, inequality, race, heritage and social movements shape identities and places across borders, supported by qualitative, quantitative and historical research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum visibly shifts the spatial question to global connections, migration, empire, race, heritage and transnational politics without claiming a dedicated geography sequence.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces most planning, design, environmental-engineering and domestic urban-governance content with empire, international relations, global political economy, migration-related inequality, race, heritage and transnational cultural histories. It differs by at least nine courses from each other alternative.
progression: Sociology, politics, history and research foundations precede global political economy, international law, race, heritage, social movements and advanced transnational analysis. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Urban governance, inequality & policy
alternatives.concept: Organises sociology, politics, law, economics, psychology and communication around urban inequality, housing, institutions, public decision-making, social movements and the governance of sustainable and inclusive cities.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme centres the institutional, distributive and political choices through which cities are governed, while retaining social-research methods and environmental policy.
alternatives.distinctness: This route shifts from the closest programme’s spatial-environmental methods and the migration route’s transnational historical emphasis toward law, political institutions, inequality, housing, public decision-making, communication and inclusive-city governance. It differs from each prior alternative by well over four courses.
progression: Sociology, politics, law and research-method foundations precede comparative institutions, urban inequality, rights, governance, communication and advanced policy-facing study. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

selection.assessment: The closest programme integrates the target’s social-spatial, environmental and mixed-method core. The first two evidenced track directions after that core—migration/global development and inclusive cities—produce feasible, materially different UCR curricula. Planning sustainable cities and innovative sustainable regions are also coherent but production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: Utrecht supplies a continuous disciplinary sequence in social geography and planning, including spatial data, track-specific mixed-method research, practice work and a bachelor thesis. UCR combines strong sociology, politics, economics, sustainability, environmental science, data and research courses but does not offer the same full geography-and-planning or professional planning sequence. The UCR alternatives are related academic paths rather than equivalent credentials.
